key_insights: The NDX closed Friday on its lows, back below its 50/100-day moving averages and through trend-line support. It finished down about 550 bps on the week, its largest weekly decline since Liberation Day, led by Semis down about 11.5%.

Franchise flows showed selling pressure across Tech and AI. The desk ties it to the market re-pricing growth expectations lower, driven by Rates/Oil tensions and a growing debate on how linear the AI build-out is. GIR estimates AI capex contributes about half of S&P 500 EPS growth.
Client conversation last week centered on testing thematic and fundamental convictions after several tough months, with few 'innings' type inbounds. The calendar into year-end is compressed.

Unlike the July momentum unwind, which the desk calls largely technical after the April-June run, this episode has investors debating which overhang is most acute or solvable: earnings, elections, rates/credit, ROIC, inflation, product momentum, build-out execution or policy.

The desk finds it hard to separate the uniformly positive bottoms-up AI ecosystem signals from top-down overhangs (rates, policy, price action, law of large numbers) that the Semis multiple compression may represent.

Technicals point to possible counter-rallies in coming days, but investors have lost conviction on what the durable clearing event would be. That suppresses near-term appetite to re-gross into the same names in short order.
The week's earnings are a test: AI/Semi leaders (TTMI, LRCX, WDC) report alongside out-of-favor names (CMCSA, IBM, AT&T, INFY). Other setups clients asked about are META, SPCX, TXN and NFLX.
Low vol and Quality are working while Cyclicals lag. That has hurt consensus positioning, and the GS HF VIP L/S pair (GSTHVIPP) had one of its bigger weekly drawdowns in recent memory.

Streaks: SOX is on an 8-day losing streak (longest since 2008), R2K is down 6 straight weeks (longest since 2018), BKX is down 6 straight weeks (longest since 2008), and Consumer Discretionary has traded lower in 9 of 10 weeks.
The S&P 500 low-volatility index is up 7 days in a row (11 of 12 sessions). The Mag 7 has outperformed the NDX in 10 of 11 sessions. DIS completed a 10-day winning streak, its longest since 2013.

NDX forward P/E is back to 20.5x, the lowest since the AI cycle began in 2023, and only about a 1.8x premium to the S&P 500, the narrowest in nearly 10 years. Semis have de-rated from about 29x this summer to 17x forward P/E.
Semis are about 25% off their highs relative to the S&P 500. The desk notes 20+ years of SOX vs SPX drawdown history suggests the pullback may be near its typical depth.

AAPL is at all-time highs and just short of retaking NVDA as the world's largest company. The desk calls it the clearest beneficiary of the flight-to-safety bid within tech, with a forward FCF yield of about 3.15%, above the NDX. Its 2-month rolling correlation with the NDX is inverse for the first time in history.
A chart of the US Financial Conditions Index against a defensives vs cyclicals pair shows tighter financial conditions coincide with rotation into defensives over cyclicals.
SPXXAI (S&P 500 ex-AI) is closing the gap vs SPX as the correlation of AI names with SPXXAI reverts lower.
